arxiv-2012-08729.title: Data Trading with a Monopoly Social Network Outcomes are Mostly Privacy Welfare Damaging
arxiv-2012-08729.creator: Ranjan Pal, Junhui Li, Yixuan Wang, Mingyan Liu, Swades De, and Jon Crowcroft
arxiv-2012-08729.description: Abstract 1 abstract This paper argues that data of strategic individuals with heterogeneous privacy valuations in a distributed online social network (e.g., Facebook) will be under-priced, if traded in a monopoly buyer setting, and will lead to diminishing utilitarian welfare.

arxiv-2103-03914.title: Essentially Tight Kernels for (Weakly) Closed Graphs
arxiv-2103-03914.creator: Tomohiro Koana, Christian Komusiewicz, Frank Sommer
arxiv-2103-03914.description: Abstract We study kernelization of classic hard graph problems when the input graphs fulfill triadic closure properties. More precisely, we consider the recently introduced parameters closure number c c and the weak closure number γ \gamma [Fox et al., SICOMP 2020] in addition to the standard parameter solution size k k .

arxiv-2205-03191.title: Distribution of 3-regular and 5-regular partitions
arxiv-2205-03191.creator: QI-YANG ZHENG
arxiv-2205-03191.description: Abstract . In this paper we study the function b 3 ​ ( n ) b_{3}(n) and b 5 ​ ( n ) b_{5}(n) , which denote the number of 3 3 -regular partitions and 5 5 -regular partitions of n n respectively.

arxiv-2304-09328.title: On the Optimal Control of a Linear Peridynamics Model
arxiv-2304-09328.creator: Tadele Mengesha and Abner J. Salgado and Joshua M. Siktar
arxiv-2304-09328.description: Abstract . We study a non-local optimal control problem involving a linear, bond-based peridynamics model. In addition to existence and uniqueness of solutions to our problem, we investigate their behavior as the horizon parameter δ \displaystyle\delta , which controls the degree of nonlocality, approaches zero.

arxiv-2310-15757.title: Do Differences in Values Influence Disagreements in Online Discussions?
arxiv-2310-15757.creator: Michiel van der Meer, Piek Vossen, Catholijn M. Jonker, Pradeep K. Murukannaiah
arxiv-2310-15757.description: Abstract Disagreements are common in online discussions. Disagreement may foster collaboration and improve the quality of a discussion under some conditions. Although there exist methods for recognizing disagreement, a deeper understanding of factors that influence disagreement is lacking in the literature. We investigate a hypothesis that differences in personal values are indicative of disagreement in online discussions.

arxiv-2409-15943.title: Aspects of Hilbert space fragmentation in the quantum East model: fragmentation, subspace-restricted quantum scars, and effects of density-density interactions
arxiv-2409-15943.creator: Maitri Ganguli 1 , Sreemayee Aditya 2∗ , and Diptiman Sen 2
arxiv-2409-15943.description: Abstract We investigate a one-dimensional correlated-hopping model of spinless fermions with an East constraint. We first analytically unravel the complete fragmentation structure of this model by labeling each fragment by a unique root configuration and utilizing the transfer matrix method.

arxiv-2410-10472.title: Data informed epidemiological-behavioural modelling
arxiv-2410-10472.creator: Daniele Proverbio, Riccardo Tessarin, Giulia Giordano
arxiv-2410-10472.description: Abstract Augmenting classical epidemiological models with information from the social sciences helps unveil the interplay between contagion dynamics and social responses. However, multidisciplinary integration of social analysis and epidemiological modelling is often challenging, due to scarcity of vast and reliable data sources and because ad hoc modelling assumptions may not reproduce empirically observed patters.

arxiv-2508-06833.title: Efficient data-driven regression for reduced-order modeling of spatial pattern formation Journal: Journal of Computational Physics
arxiv-2508-06833.creator: Alessandro Alla, Rudy Geelen, Hannah Lu
arxiv-2508-06833.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Alessandro Alla, Rudy Geelen, Hannah Lu. We present an efficient data-driven regression approach for constructing reduced-order models (ROMs) of reaction–diffusion systems exhibiting pattern formation. The ROMs are learned non-intrusively from available training data of physically accurate numerical simulations. The method can be applied to general nonlinear systems through the use of polynomial model form, while not requiring knowledge of the underlying physical model, governing equations, or numerical solvers.

arxiv-2510-19203.title: Aligning Multilingual News for Stock Return Prediction CCS: Computing methodologies Natural language processing CCS: Applied computing Economics
arxiv-2510-19203.creator: Yuntao Wu, Lynn Tao, Ing-Haw Cheng, Charles Martineau, Yoshio Nozawa, John Hull, Andreas Veneris
arxiv-2510-19203.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yuntao Wu, Lynn Tao, Ing-Haw Cheng, Charles Martineau, Yoshio Nozawa, John Hull, Andreas Veneris. News spreads rapidly across languages and regions, but translations may lose subtle nuances. We propose a method to align sentences in multilingual news articles using optimal transport, identifying semantically similar content across languages. We apply this method to align more than 140,000 pairs of Bloomberg English and Japanese news articles covering around 3500 stocks in Tokyo exchange over 2012-2024. Aligned sentences are sparser, more interpretable, and exhibit higher semantic similarity.

arxiv-2602-16514.title: Atmospheric Neutrino Charged-Current Interactions at Large Liquid-Scintillator Detectors:
arxiv-2602-16514.description: Abstract In this work, we present a systematic study of the event characteristics and physics of neutrino-antineutrino discrimination associated with atmospheric neutrino charged-current interactions in large liquid scintillator detectors. This study encompasses the primary neutrino interactions, the sequential second interactions of final-state particles, and the final neutron captures.

pmc-10682531.title: Forecasting the transportation energy demand with the help of optimization artificial neural network using an improved red fox optimizer (IRFO)
pmc-10682531.creator: Yijie Liu, Gongxing Yan, Andrea Settanni
pmc-10682531.description: Transportation energy demand has a significant impact on worldwide energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions. Accurate transportation energy demand predictions can help policymakers develop and implement successful energy policies and strategies. In this study, a novel approach to predict transportation energy demand using the Artificial Neural Network (ANN) based on the Improved Red Fox Optimizer (IRFO) has been suggested.

pmc-11440893.title: Identification of quantitative trait loci for lodging and related agronomic traits in soybean (Glycine max [L.] Merr.)
pmc-11440893.creator: Bo Chen, Cheng Chai, Mingming Duan, Ximeng Yang, Zhandong Cai, Jia Jia, Qiuju Xia, Shilin Luo, Lu Yin, Yunxia Li, Nianen Huang, Qibin Ma, Hai Nian, Yanbo Cheng
pmc-11440893.description: BackgroundLodging, a crucial agronomic trait linked to soybean yield, poses a significant challenge in soybean production. Nevertheless, there has been less research on soybean lodging compared to other important agronomic traits, hindering progress in breeding high-yield soybeans. Our goals were to investigate lodging, pinpoint quantitative trait loci (QTL) linked to lodging, and forecast potential candidate genes linked to this trait.

pmc-11505251.title: Four New Sequence Types and Molecular Characteristics of Multidrug-Resistant Escherichia coli Strains from Foods in Thailand
pmc-11505251.creator: Nalumon Thadtapong, Soraya Chaturongakul, Sithichoke Tangphatsornruang, Chutima Sonthirod, Natharin Ngamwongsatit, Ratchaneewan Aunpad, Bożena Futoma-Kołoch, Anna Kędziora
pmc-11505251.description: The presence of antibiotic-resistant Escherichia coli in food is a serious and persistent problem worldwide. In this study, 68 E. coli strains isolated from Thai food samples were characterized. Based on antibiotic susceptibility assays, 31 of these isolates (45.59%) showed multiple antibiotic resistance (MAR) index values > 0.2, indicating high exposure to antibiotics.

pmc-11629461.title: To activate NAD(P)H oxidase with a brief pulse of photodynamic action
pmc-11629461.creator: Xiao Bing Xie, Yu Shu, Zong Jie Cui
pmc-11629461.description: Reduced nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate [NAD(P)H] oxidases (NOX) are a major cellular source of reactive oxygen species, regulating vital physiological functions, whose dys‐regulation leads to a plethora of major diseases. Much effort has been made to develop varied types of NOX inhibitors, but biotechnologies for spatially and temporally controlled NOX activation, however, are not readily available.

pmc-11733810.title: Congenital Heart Disease Surgery in Low-Resource Settings
pmc-11733810.creator: Bistra Zheleva, Liesl Zühlke
pmc-11733810.description: Corresponding Author In high-income countries, survival from congenital heart disease (CHD) has reached over 90%, and morbidity is improving with the advances in specialized medicine and chronic disease management. However, these advances have not been reflected in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs).

pmc-12567388.title: From Bioinformatic Modeling to Clinical Observation: Potential Implications of Ribosomal RNA Folding in Blastocystis sp. Isolates from Symptomatic and Asymptomatic Carriers
pmc-12567388.creator: Fernando Martínez-Hernández, Arony Martínez, Cecilia Zampedri, Mirza Romero-Valdovinos, Carlos Jiménez-Gutiérrez, Karina Flores-Martínez, Armando Trejo-Chávez, Guiehdani Villalobos, Pablo Maravilla
pmc-12567388.description: Here, 18S-rDNA sequences of Blastocystis sp., previously documented from symptomatic (cases) and asymptomatic (controls) carriers, were analyzed to determine their population structure, predict their secondary structure, and examine their interactions with ribosomal proteins (Bud23, RPS5, and RPS18). Phylogenetic and population differentiation analyses were performed using STRUCTURE software V2.3.4.

pmc-12969395.title: From phase 1 to approval: lymphoma’s long road
pmc-12969395.creator: Mark Hertzberg
pmc-12969395.description: period (2000-2019). The findings offer a valuable lens through which to assess the evolving landscape of lymphoma drug development and the barriers that persist to impede progress. Luo et al evaluated 651 distinct agents tested in B-cell and T-cell lymphomas, including chronic lymphocytic leukemia across 1032 phase 1 trials, 1027 phase 2 trials, and 140 phase 3 trials.

pmc-13017244.title: Early postnatal growth predictors of catch-up growth in term small-for-gestational-age infants: a nationwide propensity-score–matched study
pmc-13017244.creator: Jinjoo Choi, Yun Jin Kim, Myoung-Jin Yoo, Jeesun Yoo, Ja-Hye Ahn, Yunsoo Choe, Seung Yang
pmc-13017244.description: BackgroundInfants born small for gestational age (SGA) are at risk for impaired growth and metabolic complications. However, the long-term effects of early feeding type on catch-up growth (CUG) in SGA infants remain controversial, and there have been no established anthropometric thresholds to predict later CUG.

pmc-13173861.title: Value of intratumoral and peritumoral radiomics based on DCE-MRI in predicting HER2-low and HER2-zero in breast cancer
pmc-13173861.creator: Min Sun, Yuwei Wang, Ruoming Li, Weining Zhao, Haiqing Yang, Lixia Zhou, Duo Gao, Shuai Quan, Zuojun Geng
pmc-13173861.description: BackgroundThe aim of this study was to develop and validate intratumoral and peritumoral radiomic models based on DCE-MRI to predict the human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) low and zero states of breast cancer(BCa).MethodsThe clinical data of 168 patients with BCa were retrospectively analysed and divided into a training set and a validation set.

pmc-13193399.title: STGAD: Self-temporal generative adversarial framework with transformer attention for unsupervised multivariate time-series anomaly detection and localization
pmc-13193399.creator: Xiao Liao, Wei Deng, Hongyue Ma, Yihan Mu, Fatih Uysal, Daniel Parkes, Abdul Ahad, Abdul Ahad, Abdul Ahad
pmc-13193399.description: Unsupervised anomaly detection in multivariate time series is important for maintaining the reliability of complex cyber-physical systems. However, existing methods often face practical challenges in adversarial stability, temporal dependency modeling, and anomaly-score calibration across datasets. We present STGAD, a dual-score generative-adversarial framework for anomaly detection and localization in multivariate time series.

pmc-13371344.title: Shared and niche-specific transcriptional signatures of macrophage aging revealed by a cross-tissue meta-analysis
pmc-13371344.creator: Ella Schwab, Eyael Tewelde, Leon Chen, Bérénice A Benayoun
pmc-13371344.description: BackgroundAging is accompanied by widespread transcriptional remodeling across tissues, yet how aging impacts different categories of tissue-resident macrophages is not well understood. Macrophages are highly specialized innate immune cells shaped by their local microenvironments, suggesting that aging may elicit both shared and niche-specific transcriptional responses.

pmc-13536237.creator: Zenaida Iordan, Diane Morfin, Marion Bernetiere, Marie Fauchet, Noël Peretti, Bérénice Segrestin, Pierre Poinsot
pmc-13536237.description: ObjectiveAnorexia nervosa (AN) is a serious illness in which more than half of all deaths are due to malnutrition.
